# speculative decoding for LLM inference: engineering brief

## TL;DR
- **Draft Model Design Matters More Than Raw Capability:** Analysis shows that a draft model's performance in speculative decoding depends heavily on its latency rather than simple language modeling capability. Hardware-efficient draft models can dramatically improve overall throughput.
- **Adapting to Domain Shifts via Online Updates:** Static draft models suffer in diverse or out-of-domain query contexts; continually updating draft models on observed user queries (via online knowledge distillation) significantly increases token acceptance rates and latency reduction.

The codebase contains several high-severity security vulnerabilities, notably unvalidated command execution and unsafe deserialisation, requiring immediate remediation of command injection in `ping_host`. ## Summary
- Overall posture: The architecture uses standard modern AWS managed services (CloudFront, ALB, ECS Fargate, RDS PostgreSQL, S3) but has critical gaps in high availability, security hardening, and resource rightsizing.

- Quickest win: Enable S3 block public access, server-side encryption, and secure transport on the user upload bucket, and configure RDS for Multi-AZ.

The 5 genres with the most tracks are Rock (1,297 tracks), Latin (579 tracks), Metal (374 tracks), Alternative & Punk (332 tracks), and Jazz (130 tracks).

## Data
| GenreName | TrackCount |
|---|---|
| Rock | 1297 |
| Latin | 579 |
| Metal | 374 |
| Alternative & Punk | 332 |
| Jazz | 130 |

## SQL used
```sql
SELECT g.Name AS GenreName, COUNT(t.TrackId) AS TrackCount
FROM Genre g
JOIN Track t ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY TrackCount DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

## Notes
- Results are ordered in descending order by the number of tracks per genre and limited to the top 5.
